summary: Aermotor tower first erected in 1932 in the Nicolet forest and moved by CCC crews in 1935; the first site is gone, and the tower still stands at Mountain.

facts.design: Aermotor LS-40 galvanized steel tower with a 7-by-7-foot cab
facts.status_note: Gone from the first site: the tower was moved in 1935 and still stands at the current Mountain site.

access.note: Refers to the moved tower at the current site, which the Wisconsin register record says is open to the public. No source describes access to the first site.

facts.agency: USDA Forest Service, Chequamegon-Nicolet National Forest

events.note: Prefabricated by Aermotor and first erected by the Wisconsin Conservation Commission at the first site. The Forest Service dates the tower to 1935.
Moved to the current site; the CCC took the tower apart, and the nomination believes it rebuilt it there.
The nomination cites a former CCC enrollee who staffed the tower in 1940.
Last fire called in from the tower, 25 April 1970.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Forest Service page says the tower was built in 1935. The register form and the Wisconsin record say it was prefabricated and first erected in 1932, then moved and rebuilt in 1935. The 1932 date is the first erection; 1935 is the move.

The Forest Service says the moved tower is about 2.5 miles north of the community of Mountain, WI. The Wisconsin record says two miles north of the community. The story uses the Forest Service figure and cites it.

notes_for_editor: Build date conflict: the register gives 1932 (prefabricated, first erected elsewhere) and 1935 (moved); the Forest Service page says built 1935. The Wikipedia infobox also says 1935. The story gives both. The link between the FFLA point Mountain – first (45.20406, -88.40867) and the nomination's first site is inferred, not stated by any source: the point is about 4.6 km (2.9 mi) east-southeast of the standing tower's FFLA point (45.21556, -88.46472), which fits the nomination's 'about two and one-half miles east-southeast'. No source gives the first site's coordinates. The access fact describes the moved tower only; access at the first site is unknown. Height is from the Forest Service '100-foot' figure; the nomination lists 99'-9" of woodwork. The latest source on the first site's piers is the 2008 nomination.
